chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Salim al-Ashall who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dog which holds upon its prey and has already eaten from it. He said: There is no problem with what it ate, and it is permissible for you.

key_terms.الصيد: Prey/game (al-sayd) — hunted animal; also the act of hunting
key_terms.الكلب: The hunting dog (al-kalb) — in fiqh, refers specifically to a trained hunting dog whose catch is lawful
key_terms.حلال: Permissible/lawful — the meat is fit for consumption
key_terms.لا بأس: There is no problem/harm — a standard jurisprudential formula indicating permissibility
key_terms.يمسك: Holds/retains upon — the legal concept of the dog maintaining possession of the hunt

ai.seo_question: Is the game still halal if the hunting dog ate part of it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a specific jurisprudential question: if a hunting dog kills game but eats part of it before the hunter retrieves it, is the remaining meat still lawful to consume? Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that there is no harm in what the dog ate and the remaining game is still halal for the hunter. This ruling relates to the Quranic verse (5:4) which permits hunting with trained animals.
